Description / Cues: Light activation for shoulder stability before pressing work; 2-3 sets of 15-20.
Safety Notes: Keep elbows soft, avoid shrugging shoulders up toward the ears.

Description / Cues: Dynamic hip mobility, 30-45 sec per direction before squatting/carrying events.
Safety Notes: Move within a pain-free range only; don't force end range cold.

Description / Cues: Light-load squat pattern to prime hips/knees before heavier work; 2 sets of 10.
Safety Notes: Keep torso upright, knees tracking over toes.

Description / Cues: Overhead shoulder mobility prep before pressing events; 2 sets of 10.
Safety Notes: Widen the grip if shoulders feel tight; never force the range.

Description / Cues: Primes the hip-hinge pattern before deadlift/stone work; 2 sets of 10.
Safety Notes: Keep a soft knee bend and neutral spine throughout.

Description / Cues: Foundational strength lift for leg and hip drive used across most strongman events.
Safety Notes: Use safety bars or a spotter at heavier loads.

Measurement Type: Weight x Reps or Max Load
Description / Cues: Builds the pulling strength that underlies stone, sandbag, and yoke work.
Safety Notes: Maintain a neutral spine; avoid rounding under near-max loads.

Description / Cues: Builds upright squat strength and the core bracing carried into carries and presses.
Safety Notes: Elbows high to keep the bar racked on the shoulders.

Description / Cues: General upper-body pressing strength that complements overhead events.
Safety Notes: Use a spotter above roughly 85% of 1RM.

Description / Cues: Baseline overhead strength before progressing to log/axle press.
Safety Notes: Brace the core; avoid excessive lower-back arch.

Description / Cues: Lift a stone from the ground onto a platform; a classic strongman event. Sample/training stones commonly run roughly 90-150kg — treat as an illustrative range, not a competition spec.
Safety Notes: Chalk or tacky is standard; a rounded back over the stone is normal technique, but keep the lift explosive to avoid stalling under load.

Description / Cues: Load a stone up and over a raised bar; tests both lifting and overhead control.
Safety Notes: Ensure clear space behind the bar; use a spotter for heavier stones.

Description / Cues: Load a sandbag from the ground onto an elevated platform, repeated for reps or time.
Safety Notes: Sandbags shift weight mid-lift; brace for the load to move unexpectedly.

Description / Cues: Similar to a sandbag load but with a smoother, rolling implement.
Safety Notes: Keep the keg close to the body to control the roll.

Description / Cues: Explosive clean of a smooth metal sphere to the shoulder; heavy grip and timing demand.
Safety Notes: Requires tacky/chalk; higher injury risk if grip slips mid-lift — build up load gradually.

Description / Cues: Lifting irregular natural stones builds grip and awkward-object strength.
Safety Notes: Inspect the stone for a secure grip surface before lifting.

Description / Cues: Carry a loaded handle in each hand for distance or time; a core strongman conditioning event.
Safety Notes: Keep shoulders back and down; avoid leaning to one side.

Description / Cues: Walk with a heavily loaded yoke frame across the shoulders/back.
Safety Notes: Use a spotter to help load/unload; keep short, controlled steps under heavy loads.

Description / Cues: Carry an irregular, hugged stone for distance; tests grip and core bracing together.
Safety Notes: Wear a shirt or padding to protect the torso from the stone's edges.

Description / Cues: Carry a loaded sandbag against the chest or shoulder for distance.
Safety Notes: Reposition the bag if it slips rather than fighting an awkward hold.

Description / Cues: Carry a loaded frame via handles for distance; a heavier variant of the farmer's carry.
Safety Notes: Keep the frame close to the body to avoid excess swinging.

Measurement Type: Weight x Reps or Max Load
Description / Cues: Clean and press a thick log implement overhead; a core strongman pressing event.
Safety Notes: The neutral grip reduces wrist strain, but brace the core hard through the clean.

Measurement Type: Weight x Reps or Max Load
Description / Cues: Overhead press with a thick, non-rotating bar; grip and stabilizer demand is higher than a standard barbell.
Safety Notes: A thick bar reduces achievable load versus a barbell press — adjust expectations accordingly.

Description / Cues: One-arm overhead press of a heavy, thick-handled dumbbell; tests balance and unilateral core strength.
Safety Notes: Brace the obliques hard against the one-sided load; avoid excessive lateral lean.

Measurement Type: Weight x Reps or Max Load
Description / Cues: Press a pivoting-handle press machine overhead; more shoulder-friendly than the log press for some lifters.
Safety Notes: The fixed path reduces stabilizer demand — don't treat it as a full substitute for free-press training.

Description / Cues: Explosively toss a keg over a raised bar; tests power more than max strength.
Safety Notes: Clear space beyond the bar and keep others away from the landing zone.

Description / Cues: Drag a loaded sled forward via harness or straps; a conditioning and posterior-chain event.
Safety Notes: Keep a consistent stride length; avoid jerking the load at the start.

Description / Cues: Push a loaded sled forward; a high-output conditioning and leg-drive event.
Safety Notes: Keep a stable, low body angle rather than standing tall mid-push.

Description / Cues: Pull a vehicle for distance via a harness or rope; a signature strongman spectacle event.
Safety Notes: Requires a clear, controlled path and a spotter watching for rope/harness slippage.

Description / Cues: Builds the back strength that supports deadlift and carry events.
Safety Notes: Keep the torso angle consistent; avoid using momentum to heave the bar up.

Description / Cues: Upper-back and grip strength that carries over to stone lifting and carries.
Safety Notes: Avoid excessive kipping when weighted.

Description / Cues: Front-loaded squat variation that builds the bracing needed for odd-object lifting.
Safety Notes: Pad the bar or forearms — the front-rack position is uncomfortable at heavier loads.

Description / Cues: Lower-back and glute accessory work with minimal spinal loading.
Safety Notes: Avoid excessive hyperextension at the top of the movement.

Description / Cues: Anti-extension core strength that supports bracing under heavy carries and lifts.
Safety Notes: Stop before the lower back arches; regress to a shorter range if needed.

Description / Cues: Static hold for grip endurance; a good entry point before farmer's carries for distance.
Safety Notes: Set the implements down under control if grip fails — don't drop them uncontrolled near the feet.

Description / Cues: Pinch-grip two plates together and hold for time; targeted grip-strength work.
Safety Notes: Stand over a mat in case the plates are dropped.

Description / Cues: Core and grip endurance combined; supports the bracing needed in carries.
Safety Notes: Avoid excessive swinging; control the descent.

Description / Cues: Short, high-intensity sled pushes for conditioning between heavy strongman training blocks.
Safety Notes: Keep pushes short (10-20m) to maintain intensity rather than pacing like a distance carry.

Description / Cues: Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the finish; keep a slight lean back throughout, not a big rock.
Safety Notes: Avoid rounding the lower back to add range at the finish - stop the pull where your torso naturally stops moving.

Description / Cues: Keep elbows pinned to your sides throughout; let the triceps do the work rather than leaning on the bar with body weight.
Safety Notes: Don't let the elbows drift forward as the weight gets heavy - that shifts load onto the shoulders.

Description / Cues: A safer entry point than a free-bar squat for building leg strength - feet shoulder-width on the platform; lower until knees reach roughly 90 degrees.
Safety Notes: Never let the lower back round off the pad at the bottom of the rep; don't lock the knees out hard at the top.

Description / Cues: Pull the bar to the upper chest, driving the elbows down and back rather than pulling with the arms alone.
Safety Notes: Avoid leaning back excessively or using momentum to move the weight.

Description / Cues: The fixed bar path makes this a good option for practicing squat depth and tempo without needing a spotter.
Safety Notes: Position feet slightly forward of the bar, not directly under it, to keep the movement path comfortable for the knees.

Description / Cues: An isolation move for the quads; extend the knees fully then lower under control rather than dropping the weight stack.
Safety Notes: Avoid using momentum by swinging into the first few reps - start each set under control.

Description / Cues: An isolation move for the hamstrings; curl through a full range and pause briefly at full contraction.
Safety Notes: Keep the hips pressed into the seat throughout - don't let them lift to help move the weight.

Description / Cues: A guided alternative to the bench press for building pressing strength without needing a spotter.
Safety Notes: Adjust the seat height first so the handles line up with mid-chest, not the shoulders or the collarbone.

Description / Cues: A lever (often a bar or PVC pipe with a rope and weight attached) rotated by the wrists to roll the weight up, then lowered under control; builds forearm and wrist strength for grip-heavy lifts.
Safety Notes: Start light - this is a small-muscle-group movement and forearms fatigue and strain easily if the load jumps too fast.
